contentBlocks.text: Last week you mastered proportional relationships. This week: operations with all rational numbers, starting with adding and subtracting integers!

Adding a negative number is the same as subtracting: 5 + (-3) = 5 - 3 = 2. Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding: 5 - (-3) = 5 + 3 = 8. Think of it on a number line: adding a positive moves right, adding a negative moves left. Solve: -8 + 5, and -3 - 7.
You just added and subtracted integers, building on Grade 6's negative-number foundation! Tomorrow we'll multiply and divide them.

objectives: Add and subtract integers using the equivalence between subtracting and adding a negative
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's proportional-relationships work briefly.
2. Introduce the add/subtract-negative equivalence using the number-line model.
3. Have the child solve -8 + 5 and -3 - 7 independently.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's multiplication/division lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: draw an actual number line and count the moves for each problem
Ready for more: ask the child to write a real-world scenario matching -3 - 7 (like a temperature dropping twice)
This directly extends Grade 6's negative-number introduction into real integer operations, a genuine Grade 7 step up
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 7 standard 7.NS.1: adding and subtracting rational numbers, opening this week's operations thread from the course's own description.
